description.value: A 57-site BC Parks campground on the southwestern shore of 13 km Charlie Lake, 11 km north of Fort St. John, offering swimming, canoeing, fishing for northern pike and walleye, a playground, and disc golf; gate closes for the off-season.

address.value: 11 km north of Fort St. John, Alaska Highway at Highway 29, BC

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms this is an active provincial campground on Charlie Lake, 11km north of Fort St. John. OSM tags provide capacity (57 sites), fee status, no internet access, and a sanitary dump station. The website explicitly mentions a picnic shelter (covered shelter = true) and confirms reservations are accepted through BC Parks' reservation system. Cycling is permitted on designated roads and trails, but e-bikes are explicitly restricted to park roads only. No evidence found for hiker/biker sites, showers, potable water, food, laundry, or other amenities beyond what is listed.
concerns: OSM tag internet_access=no — no Wi-Fi or internet available at the campground
E-bikes are explicitly prohibited on park trails; restricted to park roads and areas where motorized use is permitted
Operated by a private contractor (Sandstorm North Contracting) rather than directly by BC Parks; operator contact is sandstormnorth@gmail.com
No phone number available for the campground itself; BC Parks general line is 1-800-689-9025
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active BC Parks campground with 57 sites on the Alaska Highway corridor, a logical overnight stop for touring cyclists heading through northern BC. Cycling is explicitly permitted on designated roads and trails.
enrichment_extras.notes: Sanitary dump station available per OSM tags. Pets allowed on leash but not on beach areas. Park located at junction of Alaska Highway and Highway 29.

wow_evidence: 57-site BC Parks campground on the Alaska Highway corridor... swimming, canoeing, fishing
